subject: Sentinel RFP — staged adoption roadmap, telemetry, and rollback stages
messages:
From: Evelyn O'Neal <evelyn.oneal@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up — detailed migration/rollout plan request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our RFP evaluation we need a detailed implementation and migration plan that covers: timeline by phase, integration steps (API, embedding migration, identity & routing), canary criteria and traffic ramp, rollback gates, and telemetry/alerting requirements.

Attached is the RFP worksheet where we capture vendor responses — we’d like a completed timeline matrix and the architecture diagram by next Tuesday (2025-07-29).

Can you confirm you can provide: 1) a stage-by-stage timeline with estimated effort and owners, 2) acceptable downtime/maintenance windows and rollback triggers, and 3) a sample canary runbook we can review?

Also include any prerequisites from our side (network, firewall, KMS, data residency). We’ll need these items for procurement and security review.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Director, Platform Integrations
Sentinel Health

Attachment: Sentinel_RFP_Q3_Rollout_Template.xlsx (excel worksheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn O'Neal <evelyn.oneal@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — detailed migration/rollout plan request

Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear ask and the template. We can deliver the requested plan and a sample canary runbook. I’ve attached an integration diagram and a prefilled timeline outline for your review; we’ll fill the worksheet you attached with finer granularity by 2025-07-29.

High-level commitments:
- Phase 0 (Prep, 1–2 weeks): network setup, KMS integration, Admin onboarding, baseline telemetry. Owner: Sentinel infra + Redwood solutions eng.
- Phase 1 (Pilot, 2–3 weeks): Non-prod model routing, prefix/KV caching enabled, small traffic pilot (1–5% of calls). Canary criteria: latency within 15% of baseline, error rate <0.5% sustained over 1 hour, no functional regressions in smoke prompts.
- Phase 2 (Gradual ramp, 3–6 weeks): progressive traffic shift (5% → 50%) across routes with telemetry escalation gates.
- Phase 3 (Full cutover & optimization, 2–4 weeks): full traffic, enable aggressive batching/quantization suggestions, post-cutover tuning.

Rollback gates (examples):
- Immediate rollback if error spike >2% and not resolved within 15 minutes.
- Rollback if token-cost regression exceeds 30% compared to baseline for 24 hours.

Prerequisites we need from Sentinel:
- VPC peering/firewall rules allowing Redwood egress IPs (we'll provide list)
- KMS access for optional envelope encryption (or HSM integration windows)
- Sample prompt set and eval cases for quality regression tests
- Contact for on-call coordination during canary windows (2 engineers on each side)

I’m looping in internal owners to prepare a detailed worksheet and the canary runbook.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-integration-diagram.png, SENT-RFP-Ack.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFP follow-up — detailed migration/rollout plan request

Team — forwarding Sentinel's RFP request (see attached worksheet). They want a detailed timeline, canary runbook, and tech prerequisites by 2025-07-29.

What I need from you for the response:
- Priyom: a concise non-prod→prod integration checklist (API keys, model pinning, routing policies, prefix/KV cache warmup) and estimated engineering days per phase.
- Ben: proposed SRE on-call coverage and telemetry/alerting thresholds (latency p95 targets, error thresholds, escalation playbook).
- Laura: commercial notes — recommended maintenance windows, acceptable SLA exceptions during pilot, and any billing impacts for double-writing or shadow testing.

Draft outline I will include in the worksheet:
1) Preparatory tasks (network/KMS/list of IPs) — 1–2 weeks
2) Non-prod pilot — test harness + 2-week smoke + metrics review
3) Controlled ramp — staged traffic increases with checkpoints every 48 hours
4) Full cutover + optimization

Key canary success criteria (we will include specifics in runbook):
- Functional regression: zero critical failures across 200 sample prompts
- Performance: p95 latency <= baseline p95 * 1.15
- Cost: unit cost deviation < 30% for first 72 hours

Please reply in-thread with your bullets by EOD Wednesday (2025-07-23). I’ll consolidate and return to Evelyn.

Thanks —
Karthik

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 08:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP follow-up — detailed migration/rollout plan request

Karthik — quick technical bullets below; happy to expand into the worksheet.

Prep / Phase 0 (3–7 days)
- Provide Redwood egress IP CIDR list and the specific ports (443) + required firewall ACLs.
- Exchange service account keys and create dedicated Redwood service principal in Sentinel IAM.
- KMS: either grant envelope key access or schedule HSM handoff window.
- Provide sample prompt corpus (50–200 examples) and a subset of high-sensitivity prompts for redaction testing.

Phase 1 (Pilot — 10–14 days)
- Deploy to Sentinel staging environment with model pinned to X-1 (stable variant).
- Enable prefix/KV caching in read-only mode; warm-up caches with synthetic replay workload.
- Shadow traffic: mirror 100% calls but return from Sentinel's current provider; measure delta.
- Canary run: route 1–3% production traffic to Redwood for 48–72 hours.
- Acceptance gates: p95 latency within 15%, error rate <0.5%, no critical prompt failures.

Phase 2 (Staged ramp — 3–6 weeks)
- Increase to 10% → 30% → 60% over step windows of 48–72 hours with mandatory post-step metric review.
- Introduce batching and quantization profiles once load is stable.

Phase 3 (Cutover & optimization — 2 weeks)
- Full traffic shift during a planned maintenance window (2–4 hours), with immediate rollback capability.
- 7-day intensive monitoring: cost, latency, quality regressions; weekly sync.

Rollbacks & Safeguards
- Automated rollback triggers (integrated with Redwood routing): sustained error rate >1% for 15 minutes OR functional failure on >1% of smoke prompts in 30 minutes.
- Manual holdpoint: at each ramp step, Sentinel PM signs off based on runbook checklist.

Engineering estimates (rough)
- Phase 0: 2–3 engineer-days (solutions + infra contact)
- Phase 1: 5–8 engineer-days (setup, runbook, initial validation)
- Phase 2: 4–6 engineer-days across ramps (observability tuning + fixes)
- Phase 3: 2–3 engineer-days support during cutover

I’ll format this into the worksheet and paste canary runbook excerpts.

— Priyom
Senior Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn O'Neal <evelyn.oneal@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — detailed migration/rollout plan request

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the internal notes. The plan looks reasonable and aligns with our risk tolerance for pilot + staged ramp. A few clarifying items before we finalize the worksheet:

1) For the shadow traffic step — can Redwood provide an automated diff report that highlights semantic drift on a per-prompt basis and surface the top 10 regressions by category? We need that for our QA board.
2) During Phase 2 ramp, what is your recommended maximum per-step duration if we need to pause for remediation (we prefer shorter steps if fixes are quick).
3) Please add explicit on-call escalation contacts for Redwood during pilot windows (including phone escalation).

Assuming you can add those items to the worksheet, we should be able to accept the timeline and proceed to procurement review. Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call Thursday (2025-07-31) at 11:00 PT?

Thanks —
Evelyn
Director, Platform Integrations
Sentinel Health
